types.name: Cloudflare Email Service
types.description: Built into Cloudflare Workers. Sends with this Worker’s email binding, so there’s no API key. Email Routing delivers incoming mail.

fields.label: Binding name
fields.help: The [[send_email]] binding in wrangler.toml. Leave as EMAIL.

types.eventsSetup: Bounce messages and spam reports that come back to the sender are read automatically.
types.outboundSetup: In the Cloudflare dashboard open Email Service → Email Sending and onboard your domain (Cloudflare adds the SPF and DKIM records). Then send a test email. Incoming mail: Email Routing → catch-all → “Send to a Worker” → this Worker.

types.name: Resend
types.description: Developer-first email API. Supports sending and inbound (email.received webhooks).

fields.label: Webhook signing secret
fields.help: Optional but recommended: verifies inbound webhooks.

types.inboundSetup: In Resend, enable receiving on your domain and add the MX record it shows. Then go to Webhooks → Add endpoint, paste {{url}} and select the email.received event. Also select email.delivered, email.bounced, email.complained and email.delivery_delayed to see delivery status in Wren’s logs. Copy the signing secret into this provider. The API key needs permission to read received emails.
types.eventsSetup: In Resend → Webhooks, add (or edit) the endpoint {{url}} and select email.delivered, email.bounced, email.complained and email.delivery_delayed.
types.outboundSetup: Verify your domain in the Resend dashboard (Domains), then paste a sending API key.

types.name: Amazon SES
types.description: Amazon Simple Email Service (v2 API, raw MIME). Inbound via SES receipt rules → SNS (or S3 + SNS).

fields.label: Allowed SNS topic ARN
fields.help: Only accept inbound notifications from this topic (recommended).

types.inboundSetup: In SES, add a receipt rule for your domain with an SNS action (encoding: Base64) — or an S3 action plus SNS topic for large mail. Subscribe {{url}} to the topic (HTTPS); Wren confirms the subscription automatically. For S3, the IAM user also needs s3:GetObject on the bucket.
types.eventsSetup: Create a configuration set (or identity notifications) that sends Bounce, Complaint and Delivery events to an SNS topic, and subscribe {{url}} to it over HTTPS.
types.outboundSetup: Verify your domain identity in SES (Easy DKIM), request production access, and create an IAM user allowed to call ses:SendEmail / ses:SendRawEmail.

types.name: Postmark
types.description: Fast transactional email with excellent deliverability and inbound processing.
types.inboundSetup: In your Postmark server, open the Inbound stream → Settings and set the webhook URL to {{url}}. Enable “Include raw email content in JSON payload” for best fidelity. Point your MX to inbound.postmarkapp.com (or forward to the inbound address Postmark gives you).
types.eventsSetup: In Postmark → your server → Webhooks, add {{url}} and tick Delivery, Bounce and Spam Complaint.
types.outboundSetup: Add and verify a Sender Signature or Domain (DKIM + Return-Path) in Postmark, then copy the server API token.

types.name: SendGrid (Twilio)
types.description: Twilio SendGrid Mail Send v3 API and Inbound Parse webhooks.

fields.label: Event webhook verification key
fields.help: Optional: the public key from Event Webhook → Signature Verification, so Wren checks delivery events really come from SendGrid.

types.inboundSetup: In SendGrid go to Settings → Inbound Parse → Add Host & URL. Use your receiving (sub)domain, set the destination URL to {{url}} and tick “POST the raw, full MIME message”. Point the domain’s MX to mx.sendgrid.net.
types.eventsSetup: In SendGrid → Settings → Mail Settings → Event Webhook, set the URL to {{url}} and select Delivered, Bounced, Dropped, Deferred and Spam Reports. If you turn on signature verification, paste the verification key here.
types.outboundSetup: Complete Domain Authentication in SendGrid (Settings → Sender Authentication) and create an API key with Mail Send permission.

types.name: Mailgun
types.description: Mailgun Messages API (raw MIME) and inbound Routes.

fields.label: Sending domain
fields.help: The domain as configured in Mailgun.

fields.label: HTTP webhook signing key
fields.help: Verifies that inbound route posts really come from Mailgun.

types.inboundSetup: In Mailgun go to Send → Receiving → Create route. Match recipient (e.g. .*@example.com) and add the action forward("{{url}}/mime") so Mailgun posts the full MIME. Point your MX to mxa.mailgun.org / mxb.mailgun.org (EU: mxa.eu.mailgun.org).
types.eventsSetup: In Mailgun → Sending → Webhooks, add {{url}} for Delivered, Permanent failure, Temporary failure and Spam complaints. The HTTP webhook signing key verifies them.
types.outboundSetup: Add and verify your domain in Mailgun (SPF, DKIM, MX for tracking), then copy a sending/private API key.

types.name: Brevo (Sendinblue)
types.description: Brevo transactional email API and inbound parsing webhooks.
types.inboundSetup: Set up an inbound domain in Brevo (MX → inbound1.brevo.com / inbound2.brevo.com), then create a webhook of type “inbound” targeting {{url}}. Attachments are downloaded with the API key.
types.eventsSetup: In Brevo → Transactional → Settings → Webhooks, add {{url}} with Delivered, Hard bounce, Soft bounce, Blocked, Deferred, Invalid email and Complaint.
types.outboundSetup: Authenticate your domain in Brevo (Senders, Domains & Dedicated IPs → Domains) and create an API key.

types.name: Mailjet
types.description: Mailjet Send API v3.1 and Parse API for inbound.
types.inboundSetup: Create a Parse API route (POST /v3/REST/parseroute) with Url {{url}} and either a Mailjet-provided parse address or your own domain with MX → parse.mailjet.com.
types.eventsSetup: In Mailjet → Account settings → Event notifications (webhooks), set {{url}} for Sent, Bounce, Blocked and Spam.
types.outboundSetup: Validate your domain and sender in Mailjet (SPF + DKIM), then copy the API key and secret key.

types.name: SparkPost (Bird)
types.description: SparkPost Transmissions API with raw RFC 822 content, and Relay Webhooks for inbound.

fields.label: Relay webhook auth token
fields.help: The auth_token set on the relay webhook.

types.inboundSetup: Create an inbound domain in SparkPost (MX → rx1/rx2/rx3.sparkpostmail.com), then a Relay Webhook targeting {{url}} with an auth token matching the one here.
types.eventsSetup: In SparkPost → Webhooks, add {{url}} with the Delivery, Bounce, Delay, Spam complaint, Out-of-band and Policy rejection events.
types.outboundSetup: Add and verify a sending domain in SparkPost, then create an API key with Transmissions: Read/Write.

types.name: MailerSend
types.description: MailerSend email API.

fields.label: Webhook signing secret
fields.help: Optional: verifies delivery events from MailerSend webhooks.

types.eventsSetup: In MailerSend → Domains → Webhooks, add {{url}} with activity.delivered, activity.soft_bounced, activity.hard_bounced and activity.spam_complaint. Paste the signing secret here.
types.outboundSetup: Add and verify your domain in MailerSend, then create an API token with Email: full access.

types.name: MailChannels
types.description: MailChannels Email API, popular for Cloudflare Workers and shared hosting.

fields.label: DKIM domain
fields.help: Optional: sign with your own DKIM key.

types.eventsSetup: In the MailChannels console → Webhooks, add {{url}} for delivered, hard-bounced, soft-bounced and complained events.
types.outboundSetup: Create an API key in the MailChannels console and add the _mailchannels TXT “Domain Lockdown” record for your domain.

types.name: SMTP2GO
types.description: SMTP2GO HTTP API with raw MIME.
types.eventsSetup: In SMTP2GO → Settings → Webhooks, add {{url}} with the Delivered, Bounce, Reject and Spam events.
types.outboundSetup: Verify your sender domain in SMTP2GO and create an API key with the “Emails” permission.

types.name: ZeptoMail (Zoho)
types.description: Zoho ZeptoMail transactional email API.

fields.label: Send Mail token
fields.help: Paste the token with or without the “Zoho-enczapikey” prefix.

types.eventsSetup: In ZeptoMail → Mail Agent → Webhooks, add {{url}} with Hard bounce, Soft bounce and Feedback loop events.
types.outboundSetup: Add and verify your domain in ZeptoMail (SPF/DKIM), then copy the Send Mail token from your Mail Agent.

types.name: Elastic Email
types.description: Elastic Email v4 transactional API.
types.eventsSetup: In Elastic Email → Settings → Notifications, add {{url}} as the webhook URL and tick Sent, Error (bounces) and Abuse reports.
types.outboundSetup: Verify your domain in Elastic Email (SPF, DKIM, tracking) and create an API key with “Send Email” access.

types.name: Mailtrap
types.description: Mailtrap Email Sending API (transactional or bulk stream).
types.eventsSetup: In Mailtrap → Sending Domains → Webhooks, add {{url}} with Delivery, Bounce, Soft bounce, Reject and Spam.
types.outboundSetup: Verify your sending domain in Mailtrap and create an API token for it.

types.name: Scaleway TEM
types.description: Scaleway Transactional Email (EU-hosted).
types.eventsSetup: In Scaleway TEM → Webhooks, send the delivered, dropped, deferred, mailbox-not-found, blocklisted and spam events to a Topics and Events topic, and subscribe {{url}} to it over HTTPS.
types.outboundSetup: Add and verify your domain in Scaleway TEM, then create an API key with TransactionalEmailFullAccess.

types.name: SMTP relay
types.description: Any SMTP server: Gmail / Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Fastmail, Zoho, iCloud, Postfix, or a provider’s SMTP endpoint.
types.eventsSetup: Bounce messages and spam reports that come back to the sender are read automatically.
types.outboundSetup: Use an app password where your provider requires one (Gmail, iCloud, Fastmail). The From address must be allowed by the SMTP account.

types.name: Cloudflare Email Service (API token)
types.description: Send through the Email Sending REST API, for example from another Cloudflare account. Most setups should use the built-in Cloudflare Email Service instead.

fields.label: Account ID
fields.help: Found in the Cloudflare dashboard sidebar.

fields.label: API token
fields.help: A token with the Email Sending “Send” permission for this account.

types.eventsSetup: Bounce messages and spam reports that come back to the sender are read automatically.
types.outboundSetup: Onboard your domain under Email Service → Email Sending in the Cloudflare dashboard, then create an API token that can send email.

types.name: Postal (self-hosted)
types.description: Postal open-source mail server — send raw MIME via its API and receive via HTTP endpoints.
types.inboundSetup: In Postal add an HTTP Endpoint with URL {{url}} and format “Raw message”, then a route for your address(es) pointing to it.
types.eventsSetup: In Postal → your mail server → Webhooks, add {{url}} with MessageSent, MessageDelayed, MessageDeliveryFailed and MessageBounced.
types.outboundSetup: Create a mail server and an API credential in Postal, and add the domain with its DNS records.

types.name: Custom HTTP webhook
types.description: POST every outgoing message as signed JSON to your own endpoint; accept generic JSON inbound.

fields.label: Authorization header
fields.help: Optional value sent as the Authorization header.

types.inboundSetup: POST JSON to {{url}} — either {"raw": "<base64 RFC 822>", "base64": true, "rcptTo": [...]} or {"from","to","cc","subject","text","html","headers","attachments":[{"filename","contentType","content"(base64)}]}.
types.eventsSetup: Your endpoint can POST delivery status to {{url}} as {"events": [{"messageId", "type": "delivered" | "bounced" | "complained" | "delayed", "recipients": [...], "permanent": true}]}.
types.outboundSetup: Wren POSTs JSON {from,to,cc,bcc,envelope,subject,text,html,headers,messageId,raw(base64),attachments[]}. Respond 2xx (optionally with {"id": "…"}).

types.name: Raw MIME (HTTP)
types.description: Accept original RFC 822 messages over HTTP — for MTA pipes (Postfix, Exim), scripts, or custom workers.
types.inboundSetup: POST the message bytes to {{url}} with Content-Type: message/rfc822 and optional X-Rcpt-To / X-Mail-From headers. Postfix example: curl -sf --data-binary @- -H "Content-Type: message/rfc822" -H "X-Rcpt-To: ${recipient}" {{url}}

types.name: Forward Email
types.description: Receive through forwardemail.net webhooks (privacy-focused, open-source forwarding).
types.inboundSetup: Add a TXT record forward-email=<address>:{{url}} (or configure the webhook in your Forward Email dashboard).

types.name: CloudMailin
types.description: Receive through CloudMailin (JSON Normalized or Raw format).
types.inboundSetup: Set your CloudMailin address target to {{url}} using the “JSON (Normalized)” or “Multipart (Raw)” format.

types.name: Log only (testing)
types.description: Pretends to send: records the message in the server log. Useful for trying Wren without credentials.
types.outboundSetup: Nothing is delivered to external recipients. Local recipients on this server still receive mail.
